\begin{proof}
Let $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ and $(\mathcal{G}_n)$ be objects of
$\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})$. A morphism of pro-objects
$\alpha$ from $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ to $(\mathcal{G}_n)$ is given
by a system of maps
$\alpha_n : \mathcal{F}_{m(n)} \to \mathcal{G}_n$ compatible with
the transition maps where $\mathbf{N} \to \mathbf{N}$, $n \mapsto m(n)$
is an increasing function (in particular $m(n) \geq n$). Since
$\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{m(n)}/\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F}_{m(n)}$
and since $\mathcal{G}_n$ is annihilated by $\mathcal{I}^n$
we see that $\alpha_n$ induces a map $\mathcal{F}_n \to \mathcal{G}_n$.
\end{proof}
